chapter: Buffalo, Lunceford, Lil Armstrong and Stuff Smith
title: Stuff's small group at the Silver Grill and the move to the Onyx Club
summary: Back in Buffalo Stuff hired him for his quartet at the Silver Grill; Dick Stabile heard the group and arranged for them to open at the Onyx Club in New York on February 4, 1936.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Stayed a couple of months and went back to Buffalo, and when I get back to Buffalo, here's Stuff, and he calls me and says, "Hear you just got in." And I said yeah. He said, "Okay, if you ain't doing anything I'd like for you to come out here. I've got a little group out here. I've got myself and -- I've got four rhythm and myself."
A place called the Silver Grill in --

And so I went on out there and worked with him there for, oh, a few months, until Ben Bernie and Dixie Beal, I think, come through there, and so Dixie listened to the group and said, "How'd you guys like to go to New York?" "Yeah." So he said, "Okay, I'll talk to the fellow in the

Onyx Club and tell him," because, because they knew that a group called Farley and Raleigh are coming out, they're going to California, and he said, "He's looking for a group to go in there." So, in the meantime he come down to hear the band, and we opened up there on February the 4th, 1936, and stayed there about 18 months, you know. And then Stuff had this little number, "Eyes of Mud," == "I'll Be A Moppin""
And it was a big hit for him.
